parole.testo: Borrowing from older Low German Appelsina and in some dialects older Dutch appelsien. Equivalent to äpple (“apple”) + Kina (“China”).

parole.significato: type of pullover blouse, originally worn by sailors, but now usually more loose-sitting and with a wide opening
parole.testo: From Low German buserun, busserun, from Dutch boezeroen, from French bourgeron. Compare Danish busseronne, Norwegian busserull.

parole.significato: a curtain (in front of a window)
parole.testo: From Low German Gardine, from Early Modern Dutch gardine (contemporary Dutch gordijn), from French courtine, from Old French cortine, from Medieval Latin cōrtīna (“curtain”), from Latin cohors.
Borrowed from Low German kalkûn or Dutch kalkoen, nominalisation of kalkûnsche höner or kalkoensche haan "hen from Calicut" (modern Kozhikode, India). Doublet of kalikå.
Borrowed from Low German klüver or Dutch kluiver, from kluif. Cognate of German Klüver, Finnish klyyvari, Danish klyver.
